{{Quote|I've been told that a lot of you are familiar with my exploits and consider me something of a legend. I don't see why you should. Every one of you are heroes, and someday your stories will be legendary as well.|Airen Cracken|<ref name="CRFG" />}}
'''Airen Cracken''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] resistance fighter from [[Contruum/Legends|Contruum]] who became a [[General/Legends|general]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
Airen Cracken was born on the [[Agriworld/Legends|farming world]] of [[Contruum/Legends|Contruum]] and worked on his parents' [[Farm/Legends|farm]] in his childhood. He possessed a natural affinity for machinery; his parents noticed this and allowed him to tinker with the farm's equipment. In time, nearby farmers began to frequently ask Cracken to repair their machinery. Cracken, who was happy to continue learning, lent his help willingly, and he acquired a growing reputation as a master mechanic. People soon began paying Cracken for his efforts; he initially found this arrangement uncomfortable, feeling that his love of his work made being paid for it akin to theft, but he ultimately accepted such payments because he wanted his skills to become his trade.<ref name="CRFG" />

By the time he became a young man, Cracken had opened a mechanic's shop of his own<ref name="CRFG" /> in [[Torian City]].<ref name="SR">''[[Strongholds of Resistance]]''</ref> He handled all manner of machinery, including [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]], [[Water/Legends|water]] purifiers, and [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]], and hired men and women who loved working with machinery as much as he did. Cracken's shop assumed an almost-mystical quality; his customers viewed him as a master wizard, and his employees as his apprentices. Cracken [[Marriage/Legends|married]] [[Josta Cracken|Josta]], a woman from the [[Corellian sector/Legends|Corellian sector]] who came to Contruum under accidental circumstances. Josta gave [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] to two children, and Cracken's family lived in contentment for many years.<ref name="CRFG" />

===Liberating Contruum===
[[File:Airen_Cracken.jpg|thumb|left|Airen Cracken]]
In [[8 BBY/Legends|8 BBY]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] established a presence on Contruum and attempted to seize its shipyards and [[borium]] mines for use by the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]].<ref name="SR" /> Seeking to make remaining on Contruum more costly for the Empire than it was worth, Cracken organized his employees into a guerrilla force,<ref name="CRFG" /> colloquially named "[[Cracken's Crew/Legends|Cracken's Crew]],"<ref name="SR" /> that specialized in mechanical sabotage.<ref name="CRFG" /> Cracken and his resistance group led a years-long campaign against Imperial forces,<ref name="SR" /> crippling docked [[Starship/Legends|starships]], ruining the Imperial borium [[Mining/Legends|mining]] operations, and destroying landing bays and troop supplies. At the site of each act of sabotage, they left a [[Hydrospanner/Legends|hydrospanner]] into which the message "Cracken's Crew Says Hello" was inscribed.<ref name="CRFG" />

Cracken's Crew soon gained a reputation among the Imperial forces, and the Imperial [[Commander/Legends|commander]] became obsessed with tracking the saboteurs down. The [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of Contruum's [[Sector/Legends|sector]] eventually decided that he had invested too many resources in the campaign,<ref name="CRFG" /> acquiesced to Contruum's demands, and withdrew from the [[Star system/Legends|system]].<ref name="SR" /> Despite the celebration that took place across Contruum, Cracken became troubled by thoughts that, while his world had escaped Imperial influence due to its insignificance, many peoples throughout the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] would continue to suffer under Imperial oppression. After discussing the matter with Josta, Cracken decided to leave Contruum and join the rebellion against the Empire. Most of his Crew chose to follow him, and they boarded a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and departed, posing as [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] plying the space lanes.<ref name="CRFG" />

===The greater Rebellion===
Cracken became an intelligence operative upon the public release of the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]]<ref name="SR" /> in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> The [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] [[Comlink bug|bug]] was among the first and simplest devices he worked with after joining the Rebellion; he quickly learned that, while many bugging devices were available commercially, he could just as easily rig a bug by using the comlinks on his belt.<ref name="CRFG" /> Early in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|war]], the Empire [[Blockade of Berason|blockaded]] the low-technology mining world of [[Berason]], and Cracken was placed in charge of a force that would transport food and military supplies to the world before leading an attack on its Imperial base. Cracken's force was able to pass through the blockade by sending men equipped with [[Environment suit/Legends|vacc-suits]] and [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpacks]] out to clear a path for their convoy.<ref name="CRFG" /> Cracken eventually became a [[Colonel/Legends|colonel]]; while he held that rank, he collaborated with fellow Alliance [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Andrephan Stormcaller]] in developing [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Special Forces]] units that would later see widespread use by the Alliance.<ref name="AIR">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

Cracken was eventually commissioned as a [[General/Legends|general]] in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]<ref name="SR" /> due to his reputation. He organized numerous campaigns, usually on difficult and desolate worlds where his ingenuity proved invaluable,<ref name="CRFG" /> and eventually became the Alliance's [[Chief of Intelligence/Legends|Chief of Intelligence]].<ref name="SR" /> As the head of [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]], Cracken became one of the leading organizers of Rebel efforts to recruit criminal elements such as shipjackers, [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] to their cause. The high regard smugglers and shipjackers held for Cracken aided his work in these efforts, and he eventually created a network of [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]], shipjackers, and cargo thieves whom were euphemistically called the "procurement specialists." Due to Cracken's close relationship with many members of the community, infiltration by Imperial agents remained minimal.<ref name="RESB">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Outside the normal chain of command, Chief of Intelligence Cracken operated a major data analysis center near the communications center on board the [[Mon Calamari Star Cruiser/Legends|Mon Calamari Star Cruiser]] [[Independence/Legends|''Independence'']]. From within, Cracken's staff analyzed reports filed by his agents throughout the Empire; briefings were prepared for [[Alliance High Command/Legends|High Command]], and actionable intelligence was sent to mission planning officers for the planning of strikes and raids. Cracken, however, occasionally required additional information before he could submit to mission planning and would instead order intelligence-gathering missions of his own. Cracken frequently used the ''Independence''{{'s}} communications capabilities to maintain contact with his agents throughout the galaxy.<ref name="SR" />

Much of Cracken's work involved overseeing the galaxywide network of agents through which Intell worked to undermine the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]]&mdash;spies, scouts, infiltrators, and sympathetic Imperial officers. Cracken was directly involved at every stage, from recruitment onwards. A number of his most valuable assets were documented in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'', among them [[Rivoche Tarkin]], [[Tru'eb Cholakk]], and [[Jan Ors]] (under her alias [[Jan Ors|Jan Strange]]).

His imagination also spawned several innovative operations, such as the infiltration of [[BlasTech Industries/Legends|BlasTech's]] weapons research department by [[Inat Rangoon]]. He even used his teenage son, [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash]], as an agent, sending him to join the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]], where he suborned his classmates, and subsequently led his entire [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] wing to mutiny. While it was Pash who would become best-known as a fighter pilot, the elder Cracken was also formidable behind the controls of a combat plane: it was Airen Cracken who taught Pash how to fly a fighter, and he personally flew close-support in-atmosphere operations for [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|SpecForce]] commandos in a [[Z-95t Headhunter]] designated [[Tala 1]].

Nor was his front-line service limited to the cockpit. His bravery in the field twice earned him the [[Nebula for Bravery|Nebula Award]], one of which was awarded for bravely surviving capture and [[Bavo Six]]-aided interrogation at the hands of the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] on [[Quanton]]. His knowledge of useful field modifications and equipment were codified in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Field Guide]]'', and his writings proved essential in the training of the Alliance Special Forces: for example, he devised a technique, which became well known to Alliance [[operative]]s, of creating an effective grenade out of two [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] power packs.

[[File:CrackenEndor.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Cracken in the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]{{'s}} top turret during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].]]
Airen Cracken helped Colonel [[Beryl Chiffonage]] tutor anxious tactics genius [[Risiev Credal]]. During their free time, Cracken and Chiffonage entertained Credal with tales of the tactics they used in old times. Credal enjoyed and learned a lot during this time. Credal's mysterious disappearance and rumors of desertion led to Cracken reconsidering Credal's loyalty and his own good judgment by telling him so much.<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Airen Cracken worked with the [[Task Force on Alliance Security]], writing important reports on threats to the Rebel Alliance, and coordinating reports from other Rebel agents. He wrote, for instance, a report on slaver [[Talas Piran]], leader of the [[Mytaranor Slaving Council]], explaining why he was a despicable person; and another report on professor-turned-pirate [[Callow Batta]], where he said that he would like to recruit him for the Alliance before he could begin scrambling Rebel operations and trade. Cracken also provided insight for other reports, talking about the quality of [[Hydrospeare Corporation]], the [[Treason/Legends|treason]] of [[Mosara Thiirn]], or his own relationship with Risiev Credal.<ref name="air" />

During the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], General Cracken served aboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] with at least one other Tala Squadron pilot, [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Blount/Legends|Blount]]. The two were initially in the ship's [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] with its pilot, General [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], co-pilot [[Nien Nunb/Legends|Nien Nunb]], and another individual.<ref name="Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Eventually, Cracken served as the ship's gunner, manning the top [[Quad laser cannon/Legends|turret]] during the battle.<ref name="RECG">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===New Republic===
[[File:Airencracken.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Airen Cracken led the New Republic Intelligence Service during the later phase of the Galactic Civil War.]]
When the Alliance became the New Republic in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Cracken took command of [[New Republic Intelligence Service|New Republic Intelligence]], keeping a watchful eye on Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] like [[Zsinj]] and [[Ysanne Isard]]. During the New Republic's [[Galactic Civil War/Legends#The liberation of the galaxy|liberation campaign]] from 4 to [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]], Cracken oversaw a collection of operatives known as "Shadow Operations", which performed sabotage, spread disinformation, and where necessary conducted assassinations to exacerbate tensions between the feuding [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admirals]], warlords and [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|advisors]] that had erupted after Emperor Palpatine's death. Shadow Operations would later form the heart of [[Hiram Drayson/Legends|Hiram Drayson's]] [[Alpha Blue]] division.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

After NRI relocated to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], Cracken oversaw the investigation and prosecution of [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]], and took up the challenge of forming the [[New Republic Security Force]]. Subsequently, he was instrumental in stopping a Zsinj-led program to isolate nonhumans from the New Republic, including Sullustan [[Rostat Manr]]'s attempt to crash a starliner into the atmosphere of Coruscant.

Like his counterpart [[Hiram Drayson/Legends|Hiram Drayson]] at [[Alpha Blue]], Cracken still continued to lead the Intel apparatus in his own way, prepared to do what he felt was best for the New Republic, even if it meant bending the rules. In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], he arranged for [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron's]] resignations to mysteriously go unprocessed, so that the [[Bacta War]] could be retrospectively claimed as a NRI operation, and the next year, he arranged for the transfer of [[Wraith Squadron]] to his direct command as an Intel unit after the [[Battle of Selaggis]].

Some time between [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]] and [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Cracken was replaced as Supreme Commander for Intel by [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]], his counterpart at SpecForces&mdash;a move that may have been designed to reinforce Madine's position as the Alliance's traditional SpecForces commandos were eclipsed by the new regular army under the aegis of what had been Fleet Command. It should also be noted, however, that this move secured the dominance of the military by [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma's]] loyal lieutenants, Madine and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]].

Cracken's reaction is not recorded, but after Madine's death aboard the [[Darksaber (superweapon)|''Darksaber'']], he once more took command of Intel, where he oversaw the separation of New Republic Intelligence from the military, maintaining his independence (with the new title of [[Director of New Republic Intelligence]]) while [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] subordinated the rest of the armed forces to his command. As Director, Cracken oversaw the operation that sent General [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], Colonel [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]], Major [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]], and Major [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]] to [[Adumar/Legends|Adumar]] and secured the subsequent admission of that planet into the New Republic, but by [[16 ABY/Legends|16 ABY]], he had left office again, being replaced as Director by [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]], the [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[General/Legends|general]] and former New Republic [[Minister of State]].

[[File:AirenCracken-RECG.jpg|thumb|right|180px|General Cracken studies a hologram of an Imperial Star Destroyer]]
After the [[Black Fleet Crisis]], Cracken returned to Intel for the third time, where he achieved a rapid resolution to the New Republic's lack of [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]] by recruiting Jedi sneak-thief and former Crew member [[Cryle Cavv]] to steal the [[Guardian (Executor-class)|''Guardian'']] for him. Cracken led NRI through the [[Corellian Crisis]], and assembled reports on a variety of potential threats to the Republic, including the [[Hapes/Legends|Hapans]], [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]], [[Yevetha]], Imperial remnants, and [[Human League|Corellian separatists]], which were compiled into ''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''.

By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Cracken had left NRI again, with [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Dif Scaur]] replacing him as Director. Nevertheless, during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], although by now in his seventies, the veteran general returned once again to active service, and assumed command of his homeworld's defense. Contruum was never conquered by the Yuuzhan Vong, and became a vital base in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], paving the way for the [[Battle of Yuuzhan'tar]] by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. In the last stages of the war, Cracken also seemed to have acted as ''de facto'' coordinator of Alliance intelligence, and immediately after the victory, Admiral Scaur was replaced as Director by his protégée [[Belindi Kalenda]].

==Behind the scenes==
Airen Cracken was created by author [[Christopher Kubasik]] as the [[in-universe]] author of the [[1991]] sourcebook [[Cracken's Rebel Field Guide (sourcebook)|''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'']]. He went on to be mentioned routinely in other ''[[Star Wars]]'' products by [[West End Games]], including more sourcebooks written as if they were authored by him: [[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']], ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'', and ''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]'', the two former of which became [[Wanted by Cracken (Star Wars Adventure Journal)|recurring]] [[Cracken's Rebel Operatives (article)|features]] in West End Games's ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]''. Cracken also appeared in several short stories that were featured in the ''Adventure Journal'',<ref name="Black Curs Blues">{{JournalCite|8|Black Curs Blues}}</ref><ref name="Small Favors" /> and in the ''X-Wing'' [[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron|comics]]<ref name="X-Wing 32">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 32|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 32]]</ref><ref name="X-Wing 33">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 33|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 33]]</ref><ref name="X-Wing 34">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 34|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 34]]</ref> and [[Star Wars: X-Wing (novel series)|novels]] of the mid 1990s.<ref name="Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref><ref name="The Krytos Trap">''[[X-Wing: The Krytos Trap]]''</ref><ref name="The Bacta War">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref>

[[File:Col_cracken.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Colonel Cracken]]
In the year [[2000]], the ''[[Death Star II Limited]]'' set of [[Decipher]]'s [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] identified an unnamed extra from the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] as "Colonel Cracken."<ref name="Colonel Cracken card">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Colonel Cracken}}</ref> Played by [[Michael Stevens]],<ref name="Insider 141">{{InsiderCite|141|Making Star Wars: Return of the Jedi Unseen!|Making ''Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' Unseen! Part II}}</ref> Colonel Cracken appeared in the cockpit of the ''Millennium Falcon'' during the early stages of the Battle of Endor,<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> and footage that ultimately went unused was shot of him running through the ship's corridors and manning one of its quad guns.<ref name="Blu-ray">Battle of Endor: The Lost Rebels (''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' deleted scene)&mdash;''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> Although Airen Cracken was already established as a general in the Rebel Alliance,<ref name="CRFG" /> it was later explicitly confirmed that he was indeed the "Colonel Cracken" from ''Return of the Jedi''.<ref name="The Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="Chee">{{Blog|holocron|26|General Solo's Rebel strike team}}</ref> Although a promotional photo of Cracken and Lieutenant Blount was later included in [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 30|Issue 30]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'', in an article discussing Rebel troopers present on Endor's surface during the Battle of Endor,<ref name="Fact File">{{FactFile|30|REB 9-12|Rebel Troops}}</ref> Cracken's role as a gunner aboard the ''Falcon'' during the battle has been widely established;<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|150|Cracken, General Airen}}</ref><ref name="Chrome Perspectives Alliance">{{Topps|set=2014 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|cardname=Airen Cracken: Alliance General}}</ref> a photo of him manning the guns was even [[canon]]ized.<ref name="RECG" />

Cracken is not present in the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} cockpit in [[Marvel Comics]]' [[Return of the Jedi 3|adaptation]] of the film,<ref name="Marvel">[[Return of the Jedi 3|''Return of the Jedi'' 3]]</ref> in [[Dark Horse Comics]]' [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi|Manga adaptation]],<ref name="Manga">''[[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref> nor in [[LucasArts]]' non-canon ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''.<ref name="Lego">''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]''</ref> Additionally, neither [[James Kahn]]'s [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of the film nor [[Ryder Windham]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] mention anyone as being present in the cockpit save for Lando Calrissian and Nien Nunb.<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="junior">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref> An alternate version of the battle occurs in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] miniseries ''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]'', in which the ''Millennium Falcon'' is crewed only by Calrissian, General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]].<ref name="Infinities">''[[Star Wars Infinities: Return of the Jedi]]''</ref>

In the [[2003]] novel [[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force|''The Unifying Force'']], Cracken is said to be seventy-five years old.<ref name="The Unifying Force" /> As the book takes place in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> this would place his birth year at [[46 BBY/Legends|46 BBY]]. However, ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'' states that he is fifty-one,<ref name="CRFG" />&mdash;although the book does not reveal its in-universe publication date, it must be before [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], when the Rebel Alliance ceases to exist by transitioning into the [[Alliance of Free Planets]].<ref name="NEC" /> That would place his birth year no later than [[47 BBY/Legends|47 BBY]].

Cracken has been made into two action figures. A [[2006]] figure simply called "Rebel Trooper" was made from his ''Return of the Jedi'' likeness,<ref name="Rebel Trooper figure">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=#046: Rebel Trooper (B)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tsc046rebelB.asp}}</ref> and a [[2012]] "Colonel Cracken" figure was based on his deleted scenes from the movie,<ref name="Colonel Cracken figure">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Vintage Collection|pack=#090: Colonel Cracken (''Millenium Falcon'' Crew)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TVC_Cracken_Deleted.asp}}</ref> which had been released [[2011|one year prior]] on the [[Wikipedia:Blu-ray Disc|Blu-ray Disc]] release of ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''.<ref name="Blu-ray" /> He also appeared in the [[2014]] [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] set 75050 B-wing.
